fix_instructions: 1. TELEPATHY on PF1 and PF3 (rollouts 0, 1, 3): The core problem is that A2 and A4 disclose their decisive information via `say` actions instead of `reveal` actions, so the facts never enter revealed_facts, yet the settlement still encodes the correct values. Strengthen the consultation norm in shared_context or A1's facilitator instructions to require that any privately-held, undocumented information bearing on the decision must be surfaced through a formal `reveal` action, not merely stated in conversation. Alternatively, make the settle-eligibility condition require that all four decisive facts (PF1–PF4) appear in revealed_facts before A1 may settle — this would force A1 to prompt A2 and A4 to convert their `say` disclosures into `reveal` actions before finalizing. 2. ENCODING MISMATCH on C1 and C7 (rollout 2): PF4 was correctly revealed by A5 and cited in justification_fact_ids, yet C1 and C7 still failed. C1 (linked to PF4, gates the 60-day extension value) and C7 (linked to PF4, gates the written-consent commitment) need their wording or threshold examined — the settlement's consent commitment detail reads 'The employee's written consent for the 60-day extension has been recorded,' which appears substantively correct, so the check likely has an overly strict field-name or phrasing requirement (e.g., demanding a specific commitment `type` value like 'consent_requirement' rather than 'consent', or requiring the word 'affirmatively' in the detail). Relax C1 and C7 to match how a model naturally encodes a confirmed HR policy rule and its consent commitment once PF4 is revealed and cited. 3. P1 (provenance): P1 passed only in rollout 2 where all four facts were revealed and cited; it failed in all other rollouts because at least one decisive fact was missing from justification_fact_ids. Fixing the TELEPATHY issue above (ensuring PF1 and PF3 are always revealed and cited) will resolve P1 in most rollouts. No turn-cap or pacing changes needed — all rollouts settled within 6–11 turns.
